name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953 s.7 and the First Schedule, as varied by the CPF (Contribution Rate) Notification. Ordinary Wage ceiling SGD 8,000 from 1 January 2026 (Budget 2023). Senior-worker rates from 1 January 2026: above 55 to 60 total 34% (employer 16, employee 18); above 60 to 65 total 25% (employer 12.5, employee 12.5). Table 1 carries the citizen and third-year Permanent Resident ladder, Table 2 the SPR first-year graduated ladder and Table 3 the SPR second-year graduated ladder; each is a band family under its own predicate. Inside the graduated SGD 500-750 band the employee pays the coefficient on the excess over 500 and the employer a percentage of the whole wage. The published split rounds the total contribution half-up to the dollar, floors the employee share and assigns the remainder to the employer. NOT APPLIED: the SGD 102,000 Additional Wage ceiling, which needs a year-to-date wage axis the model does not have (SG_CPF_ADDITIONAL_WAGE_CEILING_UNMODELLED); a bonus is charged as an Ordinary Wage under the OW ceiling.

name: Chinese Development Assistance Council Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953 s.13B and the Chinese Development Assistance Council Fund contribution schedule published by the CPF Board — a monthly employee-borne contribution by wage band, deducted and remitted with CPF, payable by Chinese Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. Contribution is voluntary in the sense that an employee may opt out by written application to the fund; the schedule below is the default the employer must deduct.

authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953 s.13B and the Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund contribution schedule published by the CPF Board — a monthly employee-borne contribution by wage band, deducted and remitted with CPF, payable by Muslim employees, including foreigners. authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953 s.13B and the Singapore Indian Development Association Fund contribution schedule published by the CPF Board — a monthly employee-borne contribution by wage band, deducted and remitted with CPF, payable by employees of Indian descent. name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.3 with the Skills Development Levy Order — 0.25% of the first SGD 4,500 of monthly remuneration, a minimum of SGD 2 for an employee earning less than SGD 800 a month and a maximum of SGD 11.25 for one earning more than SGD 4,500. The three bands below carry the minimum, the rate and the maximum; the levy is employer-borne. A month in which no remuneration is payable attracts no levy, which is why the first band opens at SGD 0.01.
